h1: The 7 Best Roborock Robot Vacuums of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Roborock Robot Vacuums 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven Roborock robot vacuums from Saros flagship to Q7 entry, sorted by suction, mopping, docks and who each one suits.
summary: The Roborock Saros 10R is the best overall for its 22000Pa suction and edge cleaning arm. The Qrevo S Pro offers near-flagship suction for less, and the Qrevo S5V is the mid-range pick with FlexiArm edge mopping. For a first robot, the Q10 S5+ is the entry point, and the Q7 L5 is the cheapest in the lineup.
intro: Roborock's lineup is confusing because the names barely signal what you give up as you go down. The Saros, Qrevo and Q series differ less in suction than in the dock and the edge-cleaning hardware, and that is where most buyers overspend or underbuy.

We reviewed seven Roborock models on paper, ranking them on stated suction, navigation, mopping features and dock behavior. We relied on listings and owner reports, and you should read our price brackets as a guide to tier, not a quote.

products.name: roborock Saros 10R Robot Vacuum and Mop, 22000Pa, Edge Cleaning
products.verdict: Flagship suction with an arm that reaches edges and corners.
products.description:
The Saros 10R is a robot vacuum and mop with 22000Pa suction, LiDAR navigation and an edge cleaning arm. It is the flagship Saros tier.

It ranks first because it pairs the highest suction in this ranking with the most complete corner and edge coverage. Against the Qrevo S Pro below it, you gain 3,500Pa and the edge arm, but you pay the top $500+ price.

Buy it if you want the most complete cleaning and budget is not tight. The caveat is that it is the most expensive pick here.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting the most complete edge and corner cleaning.
products.skipIf: You are on a tight budget.

products.name: roborock 2026 New Qrevo S Pro Robot Vacuum and Mop, 18,500Pa Suction
products.verdict: Near-flagship 18,500Pa suction with premium dock features.
products.description:
The 2026 Qrevo S Pro lists 18,500Pa suction, LiDAR navigation and premium dock features.

It ranks second because it gets close to the Saros on suction without Saros-tier pricing. It also beats the standard Qrevo on suction, though both stay in the $500+ bracket.

Choose it if you want a strong dock and high suction for less. The caveat is that it lacks the edge cleaning arm of the Saros 10R.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting strong suction and dock features for less.
products.skipIf: You want the edge cleaning arm.

products.name: roborock Qrevo Series Robot Vacuum and Mop, Upgraded from Qrevo S
products.verdict: Mop lifting and an auto-empty dock for hard floors plus carpet.
products.description:
The Qrevo Series is an upgrade over the Qrevo S, with LiDAR navigation, an auto-empty dock and mop lifting.

It ranks third because the listing states no suction figure, and the Qrevo S Pro states one clearly. Its strength is mop lifting, which keeps wet pads off carpet.

Buy it for a home with hard floors and carpet. The caveat is that it sits in the $500+ bracket without published suction.
products.idealFor: Homes with mixed hard floors and carpet.
products.skipIf: You want a published suction number.

products.name: roborock Qrevo S5V Robot Vacuum and Mop, FlexiArm Edge Mopping
products.verdict: FlexiArm edge mopping at a sub-$500 price.
products.description:
The Qrevo S5V is a mid-tier Qrevo with FlexiArm edge mopping and LiDAR navigation, priced under $500.

It ranks fourth because it drops the top dock features of the pricier Qrevo models. It is the cheapest Roborock here that mops edges with an arm.

Choose it for FlexiArm edge mopping without top-tier cost. The caveat is simpler dock features.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting edge mopping on a mid-range budget.

products.name: roborock Q7 M5+ Robot Vacuum and Mop, Up to 7-9 Weeks Self-Empty, 10000Pa
products.verdict: 10000Pa and self-empty for up to 7 to 9 weeks.
products.description:
The Q7 M5+ has 10000Pa suction, LiDAR navigation and a self-empty dock the listing rates at 7 to 9 weeks per emptying.

It ranks fifth because the suction is roughly half the Saros, though the long self-empty window suits busy homes. It lists in the $200-500 bracket.

Choose it for long stretches between dock maintenance. The caveat is the lower suction.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting minimal dock maintenance on a budget.

products.name: roborock Q10 S5+ Robot Vacuum and Mop, 10,000Pa Suction
products.verdict: A self-empty dock and LiDAR at the lowest entry price in its tier.
products.description:
The Q10 S5+ is an entry model with 10,000Pa suction, a self-empty dock and LiDAR navigation.

It ranks sixth because it matches the Q7 M5+ on suction but lists no long self-empty window. On price, it is a $200 to $500 model.

Buy it as a first robot vacuum with core Roborock features. The caveat is that it is the entry tier.

products.name: roborock Q7 L5 Robot Vacuum and Mop Combo, 8,000Pa Suction
products.verdict: The cheapest Roborock here, with 8,000Pa and a vacuum and mop combo.
products.description:
The Q7 L5 is a compact Q-series vacuum and mop combo with 8,000Pa suction.

It ranks last because it has the lowest suction and, per our data, expects manual bin emptying. It also has the lowest price here. Think of it as a $100-200 purchase.

Choose it for a compact apartment or as a second robot. The caveat is that you will empty the bin yourself.
products.idealFor: Small apartments or a second floor.

whatMatters.detail: Pa measures suction pressure, and higher numbers pull more from carpet. Figures here run from 8,000Pa to 22000Pa. Look for the number in the title, but remember it is a manufacturer claim.
Round robots miss corners. An edge arm like the Saros 10R's or the FlexiArm on the Qrevo S5V reaches them. Check the listing for the arm name.
A self-empty dock pulls dust from the bin into a bag. The Q7 M5+ lists 7 to 9 weeks between emptying. Look for the stated interval on the listing.
Mop lifting raises the wet pad over carpet. It matters on mixed floors. The Qrevo Series lists it explicitly.
LiDAR scans the room with a laser to build a map. It suits dark rooms and keeps routes efficient. All seven here list it or the Q-series equivalent.

faq.a: Higher suction like the Saros 10R and Qrevo S Pro help. The Qrevo Series adds mop lifting for mixed floors.

faq.q: What mistake do buyers make with Roborock?
faq.a: They chase suction and ignore the dock and edge features. Those affect daily use more.

faq.q: Is the Saros worth it over the Qrevo S Pro?
faq.a: Only if you want the edge arm and 22000Pa. The Qrevo S Pro is the better value.

faq.q: How do I set up a Roborock?
faq.a: Place the dock on a wall with open space, then follow the app to map your home.

faq.q: How do I maintain the dock?
faq.a: Empty or replace the dust bag as needed. The Q7 M5+ lists 7 to 9 weeks between emptying.

faq.q: Can the Q7 L5 empty itself?
faq.a: Per our data it expects manual bin emptying, so check the listing before buying.

finalTake: The Saros 10R is the best Roborock if budget allows, and the Qrevo S Pro is the smarter value buy. The Qrevo S5V suits mid-range buyers who want edge mopping, and the Q10 S5+ is the sensible first robot. Choose by dock and edge features, not suction alone.
